decisions.summary: A compiled module read (__pycache__/*.pyc) stands for its source
decisions.why: The .pyc is derived from the source; keying by the source is keying by what was read, by content.

decisions.summary: Every Python child imports a recording sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH (system sitecustomize first), reads written as first seen
decisions.why: FR-013's 'in every Python process it started'; writing as first seen keeps a killed child's reads.

decisions.summary: Opaque predicate: git or make started with cwd in the repository is deemed NOT on the repository when it names any path outside the repository
decisions.why: FR-013: a file that started any other program against the repository is always run, since what that program read is not known. The clause 'and naming no path outside the repository' exempts git/make commands run from the repository that read it while naming an outside path - git worktree add /tmp/base HEAD (the project's own baseline recipe), git clone <repo> /tmp/x, git archive -o /tmp/x.tar HEAD - so a test whose outcome rests on what those read is skipped on changed inputs, the false skip the 'always run' rule exists to prevent. Not impossible, not implied by the request, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose: git on a tmp fixture repo is already excluded by the cwd/-C test alone. Should read: opaque unless the program's cwd (and any -C) is outside the repository AND no argument names a path inside it; Python children isolated or with recording dropped stay opaque as written.

decisions.summary: Kept only when every test of the file passed in a run not filtered by -k, a marker or a node id; a failure removes the entry
decisions.why: FR-013 'a tooling test file that passed' (the whole file) and 'a failure is never kept'.

decisions.summary: Files keyed by git blob id (changed files hashed as git would), interpreter version stored beside; kept in the common dir's l7r-cache
decisions.why: FR-013 'each by its content'; the common dir is what lets a clone's pass serve its land-tooling worktree (SC-010); the interpreter match only makes reuse stricter.

decisions.summary: Directory listings keyed by tracked and untracked entries, ignored entries left out
decisions.why: The literal rule defeats the request's purpose concretely: the worktree land-tooling builds carries none of the clone's ignored artifacts (__pycache__, generated files), so a listing compared with ignored entries never matches clone to worktree and SC-010's own case is unreachable for any test that lists a directory. D16's 'nothing it read is a file git ignores' bounds the file case. Residual seam, recorded: nothing bounds a test whose outcome depends on an ignored entry it lists but never opens.

decisions.summary: Reads of the content caches (.git/l7r-cache/) left out of the recorded inputs
decisions.why: The literal rule defeats the purpose: those cache files are rewritten as entries are added on every run, so any test touching a cached tool would never be reused; each entry is keyed by what it holds, and the caches are held transparent (output identical with cache on and off). Residual seam, recorded: a test asserting on the live common-dir cache's state rather than a tmp cache would be skipped on changed inputs.

decisions.summary: Reuse only under L7R_TEST_DEPS=reuse, set by land-tooling.sh alone

decisions.summary: quote-verbatim verdict(passage, page) in a ParseCache named by the module's code sha, keyed by passage and page-text sha256; report compared byte for byte with L7R_CACHE_OFF=1
decisions.why: FR-014: kept by passage and page text under the code version that judged it, report the same with and without the cache (SC-011); the comparison enforces the request.

decisions.summary: audit hook in each worker and a sitecustomize in every child Python note files read and directories listed, written as first seen
decisions.why: FR-013: a file records what it read in its own process and every Python process it started.

decisions.summary: a non-recording program marks the file opaque unless its cwd (and any -C) is outside the repository and no argument names a path inside it; an isolated or unrecorded Python child is opaque
decisions.why: Implements FR-013's 'a file that started any other program against the repository is always run'; it closes the previous round's hole (an outside path no longer exempts a git run in the repository). Read 'inside the repository' as any path whose git common dir is this repository's (the clone, its worktrees), resolved through symlinks, so a linked tree outside the directory counts as inside; a linked tree made outside the test file is a detection gap, not a decision the block makes.

decisions.summary: git init <dir> and git clone <src> <dst> judged by the paths they name
decisions.why: With every named path outside the repository they read nothing of it, so they are not 'against the repository'; a <src> that is this repository or any tree of it names an inside path and is opaque.

decisions.summary: git rev-parse asking only where the repository is is not opaque
decisions.why: FR-013 gives its own reason: always run 'since what that program read is not known'. A location query reads the repository's location, not its content, and reuse is keyed by content under the accepted spec, so the rule's purpose is not touched. Bounded to location options only (--show-toplevel, --git-dir, --absolute-git-dir, --git-common-dir, --show-prefix, --show-cdup, --is-inside-work-tree); any form that resolves a revision or reads refs or config (HEAD, --verify, --abbrev-ref, ...) is outside 'their kind' and opaque.

decisions.summary: sleep, true, false, echo are not opaque
decisions.why: They read nothing of the repository.

decisions.summary: a fully passed, unfiltered file's reads kept by blob id / directory entries / interpreter version; content caches left out; a failure removes the entry

decisions.summary: Move rule: a check moves to Sonnet only if all three findings-case runs hit every known finding AND no clean-case run raises a false alarm
decisions.why: Stricter than FR-024's literal 'finds every known finding moves'. Legitimate on the request's purpose: the GM asked for the measurement so cheaper models carry checks they can do; a clean run's known findings are the empty set, and the only thing a clean leg measures is false alarms. Applied literally, a Sonnet spec-fidelity that finds every real finding but returns false CHANGES REQUIRED would move, consume the five-round cap and Opus arbiter dispatches, and cost more than the downgrade saves - defeating the purpose concretely. Either result is still recorded.

decisions.summary: Tests run and their results compared with the cut off and on

decisions.summary: A bash guard/gate script under scripts/ that a tooling test starts is recorded as reading what hookdeps.py --deps derives for it, plus its argument list; a file whose every unknown child is such a script is reused

decisions.summary: Every other program a test starts (make, node, resvg, ruff, pdftotext, grep, a stand-in claude) stays always-run, recorded in R10 with seconds and reason
decisions.why: FR-021's exit is for a file whose programs' reads CANNOT be recorded or asked again. The only measured fact is that one instrument (strace) is refused; that is not a measurement that these seven unlike programs' reads cannot be recorded or asked again - and the plan itself records an argument list to make a script child known without saying why the same fails for a program whose reads are its arguments (grep over named files, pdftotext on one file, resvg on one svg). The scope is decided by an unmeasured premise, one argument stretched over seven cases. Purpose: the GM said the always-run files 'seem worth addressing' and earlier 'maybe it's just not feasible, that's fine, but it just seems worth looking at'; amendment 2's breakdown put other programs (22 test-seconds) above the bash guard (16), so the categorical carve-out leaves the larger share unaddressed. Owed: per program (or per file), a measured reason it cannot be recorded or asked again, or it is made known; only a measured cannot stays always-run.

decisions.summary: Guard suites replayed over recorded landings; a suite re-run on a dependency its cases do not reach is narrowed (never looser than executed) or split; slow suites first; nothing dropped; tests for skip/run

decisions.summary: The recursive tooling hash leaves __pycache__ out.
decisions.why: FR-028 says every file under scripts/. __pycache__ holds bytecode Python writes as a side effect of importing the scripts, derived from the .py files the hash already reads; hashing it would move the hash on runs with no tooling change and re-run the whole tree, defeating the request's own purpose (re-run only what changed). It adds no source the hash misses.

decisions.summary: Store v3 keeps reads per test node id, plus per-file (import, collection, module/class fixtures) and per-session (session/package fixtures) reads; a test is reused when its own, its file's and the session's reads are unchanged, plus its file, conftest.py chain, pyproject.toml and the plugin's code; a file whose every test is reusable and whose test list matches is not collected, otherwise collected with reusable tests deselected; a passing test is kept whatever else ran (-k, node ids); a failure keeps nothing.
decisions.why: FR-029 and the GM's item (2): per-test reads, a file imported only when one of its tests runs, and the shared dependencies FR-029 names. Charging module/session fixture reads to every test of that scope is the conservative way to record what a test actually depended on, not a return to per-file reuse of a test's own reads; SC-022 measures the outcome. The residue - a module/class fixture or import that reads the real record still re-runs its whole file on a research edit - is what D33's fixture move remedies, and a stale reuse would be worse than an extra run.

decisions.summary: After D32, the code-subject tests that still re-run 'on an edit to a research page' are listed with what they read; one reading the real tree only to have input gets a fixture, assertion unchanged; one whose subject is the repository's data keeps reading it.
decisions.why: FR-030 (accepted) covers a code-subject test that re-runs 'on edits to the repository's data'; D33 restricts the candidates to those that re-run on an edit to a RESEARCH PAGE, so a code-subject test still re-running on a spec, dev-ledger, registry or other data edit falls outside the measurement and is never moved. The GM approved item (3) 'code-only tests moved to fixtures case by case' with no research-only limit; the research edit was the motivating instance, and confining the rule to it completes the GM's thought. Fix: say the tests that still re-run on an edit to the repository's data (research pages, specs, dev records, registries, ...) whose subject is code, and keep FR-030's listing of each moved test with what it read before AND after.

decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; carries GM item (1) and FR-028 word for word, hash gap included.

decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; carries GM item (2) and FR-029 (per-test reads, shared deps, no import when nothing runs).

decisions.summary: Code-subject tests that still re-run on edits to any repository data (anything not under l7r/, scripts/, tests/ or configuration) found from kept reads, listed with reads before and after, given fixtures; data-subject tests keep the real tree

Detection by exclusion is at least as broad as the requirement. The code/data split is FR-030's own, and it is the case-by-case judgment in GM item (3).

decisions.summary: Each read's content stored once in one table; when a run records a path whose content moved, entries naming that path that this run did not re-record are dropped
decisions.why: A storage and eviction design FR-029 leaves open. It never reuses a test whose reads changed: a dropped entry only re-runs the test, which is the conservative direction. The one reuse it gives up is content that moved and then moved back. A per-node-id store keeping one entry per test would already lose that, so it does not narrow per-test reuse as the GM asked for it.

decisions.summary: PreToolUse Agent guard: a shared block of 2,000+ chars refused only when it starts after the new prompt's first 200 characters
decisions.why: FR-034 refuses a large shared block after ANY part that differs. The 200-character lead allowance exempts exactly the GM's own example - 'a unique sentence for its prompt, and then 10 kilobytes of context after that' - whenever the sentence is under 200 characters, which most are; any differing prefix makes everything after it uncacheable, so the allowance has no caching basis and guts the guard's purpose. Fix: a qualifying block passes only when it starts at offset 0 (or everything before it is identical in both prompts); drop the 200-character clause, and make the suite's GM-shape case a sentence shorter than 200 characters.

decisions.summary: guard compares a new prompt only with earlier prompts of the same agent type and model
decisions.why: FR-034 says 'an earlier dispatch of the session' with no type limit. A prefix cache is per model and begins with the system prompt, so a block shared across types or models can never be cached whatever its placement: refusing it is physically unfixable and serves none of the GM's purpose. Every case the GM described (same check, unique sentence then shared 10 KB) is a same-type, same-model pair and stays caught; ad-hoc general-purpose dispatches are one type and stay caught.

decisions.summary: a shared block that starts the new prompt passes, even against an earlier prompt of the old shape

The purpose (FR-032: static text a check repeats moves to its agent file) is kept: the contract part is still compared, and the test is red on the pre-D35 builder (the guidelines) and green after - it still catches the motivating leak.

decisions.summary: dispatch guard per type+model over the last 30 prompts; EVERY run of identical lines after the common prefix (cut back to a line start) is judged, not only the longest; a run of 2,000+ chars after any differing text is refused; a block starting the new prompt passes; AGENT_PREFIX_OK escape

decisions.why: Brings the plan in line with FR-034 as corrected by the GM-approved reopening (item 1); the rest of D37 (store, per type and model comparison, 2,000-character threshold, escape) stands as already cleared.

decisions.summary: Guard refuses any 2,000+ character run shared with an earlier dispatch of the same type and model, at any position; passes only a wholly identical prompt; single fix: the agent file; suite case 'block first' becomes refused; CLAUDE.md, docs/guards.md, docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md drop 'put it first'.
decisions.why: Everything except the scope matches FR-034 corrected and SC-027 word for word. The narrowing: FR-034 says 'an earlier dispatch of the session' and D41 compares only within the same type and model. Across types or models the system prompt and the cache differ, so no placement and no agent-file move lets one read the other's cache. Refusing there would force a move that saves nothing (physically impossible). The scope is unchanged from D37, which was cleared.

decisions.summary: Fan-out stagger: per session and agent type, a dispatch is COLD when none of its type went out in the prior 5 minutes; a same-type dispatch within FANOUT_S=5 s after a cold one is refused (send the rest next message); docs/reviews.md and CLAUDE.md say 'the first alone, the rest in the next message'; SC-028 measured.
decisions.why: FR-039: the first goes alone, the rest follow once it has started, the dispatch rules say so and a guard holds it. The timing window is how a hook that cannot see its siblings holds it (measured 2026-10-17 with a probe hook). A warm type (dispatched within 5 minutes) is not staggered because its prefix is already cached, which is the purpose.

decisions.summary: Test in tests/test_agent_models.py: no cacheTtl or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL naming an hour in .claude/settings.json, any agent file, or scripts/container/; seeded string.
decisions.why: FR-038 and SC-028 exactly: project setting, agent file, container setup, a seeded failure.

decisions.summary: Root and nested CLAUDE.md (research/, tests/, l7r/diagram/) become core plus index; long passages move verbatim into docs opening 'Load this file when:'; phrases quoted by hooks/scripts stay; tests/test_claude_md_quotes.py; independent Opus enumeration with verdicts, all non-kept/unreachable fixed, table recorded; SC-029 before/after.
decisions.why: FR-040 and SC-029 clause by clause. Keeping a quoted phrase in the CLAUDE.md that the hook names is how 'every hook message quoting CLAUDE.md still resolves'. The test is enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: subagent_cache.py --families groups the month's general-purpose launches with count and last date; each family recurring since 2026-10-10 gets a defined agent or is pointed at one, the rest recorded one-off in R17; 'research pass' becomes a defined research-pass agent (opus/medium, omitClaudeMd, research ladder's operative rules restated).
decisions.why: FR-041 and SC-030: classify each family, give a recurring one a defined agent, record the list. The 10-10 recency line reads the GM's 'any that still recur'. The table carries each family's last date, so the GM sees where it falls. Defining the agent is what FR-041 prescribes for a recurring family.

blocks: ## Amendment 6, reopened (FR-034 corrected, FR-038 to FR-041)

decisions.summary: Guard refuses a 2,000+ char block repeated from an earlier dispatch of the same type and model at any position; a wholly identical prompt passes; the only fix it names is the agent file; docs drop 'put it first'.
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict. It carries FR-034 as corrected and SC-027, which is reopening item (1).

decisions.summary: The one-first fan-out stagger, now marked superseded by D46 (amendment 7, research R20).
decisions.why: The only change to this block is the supersession note. FR-042 withdraws FR-039 and amendment 7's request says the hand-stagger costs more than it saves, so marking it superseded follows the request and the spec.

decisions.summary: Test that no setting, agent file or container setup turns on a 1-hour subagent cache, proven by a seeded string.
decisions.why: Unchanged. It is FR-038 and SC-028, reopening item (2).

decisions.summary: Root and nested CLAUDE.md cut to a core plus an index, with long passages moved verbatim to docs/*.md; a quote-resolution test; an independent Opus rule-by-rule enumeration.
decisions.why: Unchanged. It is FR-040 and SC-029, reopening item (4).

decisions.summary: --families sweep of general-purpose launches; recurring families get a defined agent, with 'research pass' becoming a research-pass agent; one-offs recorded in R17.
decisions.why: Unchanged. It is FR-041 and SC-030, reopening item (5).

decisions.summary: Fan-out stagger rule removed. A WAVE rule refuses the 4th launch of one agent type (any model) within WAVE_S=10 s, names the check-wave call, passes WAVE_OK, and does not count units fed through by the Workflow guard. Docs say 4+ of one type go through check-wave.
decisions.why: It is FR-042 (stagger removed from guard and docs) and FR-045 / SC-031 (4th of one type within about ten seconds refused, WAVE_OK passes). Counting any model is no narrower than 'of one type'.

decisions.summary: Saved workflow .claude/workflows/check-wave.js: a pipeline of typed agent() calls with schema {label, verdict, text}; a null unit re-launched once with the same prompt; declared verify steps (then:[{agentType,prompt}]) run with the earlier reply appended; returns one object per unit, NO REPLY when a unit is twice silent; a test holds the file.
decisions.why: It is FR-043 and SC-031's workflow-file test. Verify steps are declared rather than built from a reply because FR-043 already requires every prompt to be known when the run starts. Skipping the verify steps of a unit that never replied follows from 'runs after it with the earlier reply appended': there is no reply to append.

decisions.summary: Workflow PreToolUse guard. Untyped agent( refused unless GP_OK. A typed agent( of a guarded type outside check-wave is refused. check-wave's type must be a named FR-044 job (spec-fidelity excluded). Each unit and verify step is replayed through every PreToolUse Agent hook with L7R_WAVE_UNIT=1, and the first refusal refuses the run and drops its recorded dispatches. Wave dispatches pair at SubagentStop by prompt prefix and stay pending WAVE_PENDING_S=30 min.
decisions.why: It is FR-045, SC-031 and SC-033. Excluding spec-fidelity is not a carve-out: FR-044's named list never included it, and FR-045 requires guarded types outside check-wave to be refused. The 30-minute pending window is a design number that keeps the freeze from dispatch to return, as FR-045 requires.

decisions.summary: A check-wave run is refused whole, with the refusing hook's message and the unit's label, when any one unit or verify step would be refused, rather than that unit alone.
decisions.why: The Workflow's PreToolUse is the only point at which a run can be refused (R20: no Agent hook fires inside a run), so refusing a single unit means refusing the run. SC-031's 'a check-wave unit a guard of its type would refuse is refused, with the guard's own message' is still met.

decisions.summary: append-system-prompt.md gains the document's authorization, its list the document's named jobs plus claims-triage and modal-triage. test_agent_models fails when the text is missing, when a type has no agent file, or when a type is outside the list.
decisions.why: It is FR-044 and SC-032, word for word.

decisions.summary: The next real wave of 4+ checks runs through check-wave. Per-agent first-request read/write and the main-session wakes are recorded in research beside the last hand-launched wave of the same check.
decisions.why: It is FR-046 and SC-034.

decisions.summary: The first real wave's measurement is taken by `make wave-report` (scripts/measure/wave_report.py), and the Workflow guard names that target to the session at every check-wave run's start.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-046/SC-034 and the GM's 'the first real wave measured' (Amendment 7): the tool produces exactly the measurement FR-046 names (first-request read and write, main-session wakes, against the last hand-launched wave), and the guard's message only points at it - it refuses, blocks or rewrites nothing. Delete FR-046 and neither has anything left to do.

decisions.summary: No real check was owed anywhere on 2026-10-17 (research R21), so T56 (the measured first real wave) lands open until the first real wave runs; R21 carries the probe's and the month's hand-launched waves' numbers meanwhile.
decisions.why: It narrows when FR-046 is met, not what it requires: the feature lands with the measurement still owed. FR-046 and the GM's request (Amendment 7: 'the first real wave measured') require a REAL wave; measuring one at landing is impossible when no real check is owed, and manufacturing a wave to measure would itself break the 'real' the request names. The requirement is not dropped or weakened - T56 stays open, the comparison baseline is recorded in R21, and the guard names wave-report at every check-wave run so the first real wave is measured when it comes. The rule's purpose (learn what a real wave costs against the hand-launched one) is deferred, not gutted. The premise that no check was owed is stated as measured (R21, dated 2026-10-17).

decisions.summary: request_sections: the original request is everything before the first '## Amendment N' heading; a '###' under an amendment belongs to it
decisions.why: FR-047 defines the original request as what precedes the first amendment heading; folding sub-headings into their amendment keeps each amendment's words whole.

decisions.summary: answered(): per block, the earliest of its heading's Amendment N and every spec '### Amendment N' section holding an FR or SC it cites; a block with neither answers none
decisions.why: This is FR-047's 'EARLIEST of the one its heading names and every one whose spec section holds a requirement it cites'. Counting cited SCs too can only move the cut earlier, so the bundle carries more of the request, never less. 'Answers none' gets the whole request, as FR-047 says.

decisions.summary: trimmed_request(text, n): the original request plus every section from amendment n on; request-index.md lists the heading and first line of each section left out; the whole request when n is none or there are no amendment headings
decisions.why: Matches FR-047 clause for clause. Nothing after the cut is dropped, and both fallbacks give the whole request.

decisions.summary: build writes request.md and request-index.md, and the MANIFEST names request-index.md
decisions.why: FR-047 requires request-index.md. Naming it in the MANIFEST is how the reviewer learns it exists.

decisions.summary: Tests on a fixture feature cover only: the newest amendment's block, an earlier amendment's block, an original-plan block, and no amendments; the measured cut on 383's own bundle goes in R22
decisions.why: SC-035 names a fifth case: 'a block headed with a later amendment that cites an earlier one's requirement' must carry the earlier amendment and every later one. The plan's list leaves it out, and none of the four cases listed exercises the cross-citation path of answered() (the 'every spec section holding a requirement it cites' half of FR-047's EARLIEST rule). That path exists so a later block correcting an earlier requirement still carries the earlier amendment's words, and the GM asked for exactly this trim. None of MODE 1's grounds applies: the test is not impossible, the request does not imply leaving it out, and including it does not defeat the purpose. Fix: add the cross-citation fixture case (a block headed Amendment k that cites an FR/SC from an earlier amendment j's spec section carries amendment j and every one after it, with only sections before j in request-index.md).

decisions.summary: request_sections splits request.md into the original request (before the first '## Amendment N') and amendment sections, a ### under one belonging to it
decisions.why: FR-047 defines the original request as what comes before the first amendment heading and carries amendment sections whole; treating subheadings as part of their amendment is the mechanism, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: answered(): per block the earliest of its heading's Amendment N and every spec Amendment section holding an FR/SC it cites; a block with neither answers none
decisions.why: Restates FR-047's rule exactly (EARLIEST of heading and cited requirements' sections; none -> whole request).

decisions.summary: trimmed_request(text, n): original + every section from n on, index of heading and first line of each left out; whole request when n is none or no amendment headings
decisions.why: FR-047 and SC-035 verbatim: nothing after the earliest answered amendment is dropped; whole request in both fallback cases.

decisions.summary: build writes request.md and request-index.md; MANIFEST names request-index.md
decisions.why: FR-047 requires request-index.md in the bundle; naming it in the MANIFEST lets the reviewer find it.

decisions.summary: Fixture tests: newest amendment's block, an earlier one's, a later-headed block citing an earlier amendment's requirement (carries that earlier amendment on, index lists only sections before it), an original block, no amendments; measured cut on 383's own bundle in research R22
decisions.why: The changed text adds the later-headed-cites-earlier case, which SC-035 names explicitly; every case enforces FR-047/SC-035 and nothing beyond them. The R22 measurement is the 'measured on the bundle' SC-035 asks for.
